description:
## Goal

Build the observable stub infrastructure so that Rung 2 tests can mount components
that call `use_observable/3` without starting real GenServers.

This ticket delivers:
1. `Filament.Test.StubObservable` — a GenServer using `Filament.Observable.GenServer`
   that proxies to a user-supplied function
2. `Filament.Test.Stub` — public API: `start/2`, `push/2`
3. `observable_stubs :: map()` field added to `Filament.RenderContext`
4. One-line change to `Filament.Hooks.use_observable/3` to resolve servers through stubs
5. Tests for the stub mechanism in isolation

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await
guidance. Do not improvise.

---

## Prerequisites

- `Filament.Observable.GenServer` macro (Track D, flm-hom.2) must be merged
- `Filament.Hooks.use_observable/3` (Track D, flm-hom.4) must be merged
- `Filament.RenderContext` struct (Track C, flm-oue.1) must be merged

Files modified by this ticket:
- `lib/filament/render_context.ex` — add `observable_stubs` field
- `lib/filament/hooks.ex` — one-line stub resolution in `use_observable/3`

Files created by this ticket:
- `lib/filament/test/stub_observable.ex`
- `lib/filament/test/stub.ex`
- `test/filament/test/stub_test.exs`

---

## 1. Filament.RenderContext — add observable_stubs field

FILE: lib/filament/render_context.ex
(add field to existing struct from C1 alongside owner_pid, fiber, hook_index, etc.)

Add field: `observable_stubs :: %{term() => pid()}`
Default: `%{}`

```elixir
defstruct [
  # ... all existing fields from C1 and E3 ...
  observable_stubs: %{}    # new in F4 — maps server identity to stub pid
]
```

Update `@type t` to include `observable_stubs: %{term() => pid()}`.

This field is `%{}` in all production code paths. The empty-map check in
`use_observable/3` costs a single `Map.get` per hook call — acceptable.

---

## 2. Filament.Hooks.use_observable/3 — stub resolution

FILE: lib/filament/hooks.ex
(one-line addition to the existing implementation from D4)

At the top of `use_observable/3`, after reading `ctx`, add stub resolution:

```elixir
def use_observable(server, request \\ nil, opts \\ []) do
  project = Keyword.get(opts, :project, &Function.identity/1)
  ctx = current_context()
  # Resolve stubs: if a stub is registered for this server, use it instead
  server = Map.get(ctx.observable_stubs, server, server)
  slot_index = ctx.hook_index
  # ... rest of D4's implementation unchanged ...
end
```

This single line makes stub injection transparent to components. A component that
calls `use_observable(CartServer, ...)` gets the stub when one is registered under
`CartServer`, and the real server otherwise. Production RenderContext always has
`observable_stubs: %{}` so `Map.get` returns `server` unchanged.

---

## 3. Filament.Test.StubObservable

FILE: lib/filament/test/stub_observable.ex

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Test.StubObservable do
  @moduledoc false

  use Filament.Observable.GenServer

  def start_link(opts) do
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts)
  end

  @impl GenServer
  def init(opts) do
    stub_fn = Keyword.fetch!(opts, :stub_fn)
    {:ok, %{stub_fn: stub_fn, last_state: nil}}
  end

  @impl Filament.Observable
  def handle_subscribe(request, _subscriber, state) do
    initial = state.stub_fn.(request)
    {:ok, initial, %{state | last_state: initial}}
  end

  # Push a new state to all subscribers (called by Filament.Test.Stub.push/2)
  def handle_call({:push, new_state}, _from, state) do
    notify_observers(new_state)
    {:reply, :ok, %{state | last_state: new_state}}
  end

  # Read back the last state (useful in tests to assert side effects)
  def handle_call(:state, _from, state) do
    {:reply, state.last_state, state}
  end
end
```

NOTE: `lib/filament/test/` directory must be included in the compiled sources in
`mix.exs`. Check whether `:test_support` compilation paths are configured or whether
this file should live under `test/support/` instead. If `test/support/` is used,
update `mix.exs` `elixirc_paths/1` for the `:test` env accordingly. Do not put test
support modules in `lib/` if your project convention uses `test/support/`. Check the
existing `mix.exs` (in `filament/mix.exs`) to determine the correct placement before
creating the file. If there is a conflict about placement, stop and comment.

## 4. Filament.Test.Stub

FILE: (same location decision as StubObservable above)

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Test.Stub do
  @moduledoc """
  Convenience API for creating and driving observable stubs in tests.

  Usage in mount opts:
      stub: [{CartServer, fn _req -> %{items: [], total: 0} end}]

  This creates a StubObservable for CartServer. Components calling
  use_observable(CartServer, ...) receive the stub's value instead.

  To push an update after mount:
      Filament.Test.Stub.push(stub_pid, %{items: ["x"], total: 10})
  """

  alias Filament.Test.StubObservable

  @doc """
  Start a stub observable backed by `stub_fn`.
  `stub_fn` receives the subscription request and returns the initial value.

  Returns `{:ok, pid}`.
  """
  @spec start(stub_fn :: (request :: term() -> initial_value :: term()), opts :: keyword()) ::
          {:ok, pid()}
  def start(stub_fn, opts \\ []) do
    StubObservable.start_link([stub_fn: stub_fn] ++ opts)
  end

  @doc """
  Push `new_state` to all current subscribers of the stub.
  Triggers the same notification path as a real observable's notify_observers/1,
  including per-subscriber projection and change-or-bust from D3.
  """
  @spec push(stub :: pid(), new_state :: term()) :: :ok
  def push(stub, new_state) do
    GenServer.call(stub, {:push, new_state})
  end

  @doc """
  Read back the last state that was pushed to (or initially set in) the stub.
  """
  @spec state(stub :: pid()) :: term()
  def state(stub) do
    GenServer.call(stub, :state)
  end

  @doc """
  Build the observable_stubs map expected by Filament.Test.mount/2.
  Starts a StubObservable for each {server, stub_fn} pair.
  Returns {stubs_map, pids} where stubs_map is %{server => pid} and
  pids is the list of started stub pids (for cleanup in on_exit).
  """
  @spec build([{server :: term(), stub_fn :: function()}]) ::
          {stubs_map :: %{term() => pid()}, pids :: [pid()]}
  def build(stub_specs) do
    Enum.reduce(stub_specs, {%{}, []}, fn {server, stub_fn}, {map, pids} ->
      {:ok, pid} = start(stub_fn)
      {Map.put(map, server, pid), [pid | pids]}
    end)
  end
end
```

## 5. Tests

FILE: test/filament/test/stub_test.exs

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Test.StubTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
  alias Filament.Test.Stub

  test "initial value returned via subscribe" do
    {:ok, stub} = Stub.start(fn _req -> 42 end)
    sub = %Filament.Observable.Subscriber{
      pid: self(), fiber_id: :test, slot_index: 0,
      project: &Function.identity/1
    }
    assert {:ok, 42} = Filament.Observable.subscribe(stub, nil, sub)
  end

  test "push delivers update to subscriber" do
    {:ok, stub} = Stub.start(fn _req -> 0 end)
    sub = %Filament.Observable.Subscriber{
      pid: self(), fiber_id: :fiber_a, slot_index: 1,
      project: &Function.identity/1
    }
    {:ok, _} = Filament.Observable.subscribe(stub, nil, sub)
    Stub.push(stub, 99)
    assert_receive {:filament_observable_update, :fiber_a, 1, 99}
  end

  test "push with projection — change-or-bust applies" do
    {:ok, stub} = Stub.start(fn _req -> 3 end)
    sub = %Filament.Observable.Subscriber{
      pid: self(), fiber_id: :fiber_b, slot_index: 0,
      project: fn n -> n > 5 end
    }
    {:ok, false} = Filament.Observable.subscribe(stub, nil, sub)
    # Push a value that doesn't change the projection
    Stub.push(stub, 4)
    refute_receive {:filament_observable_update, _, _, _}, 50
    # Push a value that changes the projection
    Stub.push(stub, 10)
    assert_receive {:filament_observable_update, :fiber_b, 0, true}
  end

  test "Stub.build/1 creates stubs for multiple servers" do
    {stubs_map, pids} = Stub.build([{:server_a, fn _ -> :a end}, {:server_b, fn _ -> :b end}])
    assert map_size(stubs_map) == 2
    assert length(pids) == 2
    assert Map.has_key?(stubs_map, :server_a)
    assert Map.has_key?(stubs_map, :server_b)
  end

  test "use_observable resolves stub via observable_stubs in RenderContext" do
    # Set up a RenderContext with a stub registered for :my_server
    {:ok, stub} = Stub.start(fn _req -> :stub_value end)

    ctx = %Filament.RenderContext{
      owner_pid: self(),
      fiber: %Filament.Fiber{id: :test_fiber, hook_slots: %{}},
      hook_index: 0,
      new_hook_slots: %{},
      pending_effects: [],
      event_handler_index: 0,
      new_event_handlers: %{},
      observable_stubs: %{:my_server => stub}
    }
    Process.put(:filament_render_ctx, ctx)

    value = Filament.Hooks.use_observable(:my_server)

    assert value == :stub_value
  end
end
```

Run: `mix test test/filament/test/stub_test.exs`

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Filament.RenderContext.observable_stubs` field added with `%{}` default
- [ ] `use_observable/3` resolves servers through `ctx.observable_stubs`
- [ ] `Filament.Test.StubObservable` compiles; a module file exists at the correct path
- [ ] `Filament.Test.Stub` compiles with `start/2`, `push/2`, `state/1`, `build/1`
- [ ] All 5 tests pass
- [ ] Dialyzer clean
- [ ] Existing D4 test suite still passes (no regressions from use_observable/3 change)
